source_text: Ἐκείνην οὖν τὴν φλόγα διέκοπτε τῷ ὑπ' ὄψιν ἄγειν τὰ φοβερὰ τῷ λαῷ. Καὶ συσσείσει Κύριος τὴν ἔρημον Κάδης. Ἦν γὰρ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ. Τὴν ἔρημον οὖν ἐκείνην συνέσεισε τῇ ἐπιδημίᾳ τῶν πανταχόθεν λαῶν· ἥτις, διὰ τὸ μετανοεῖν τοὺς ἐρχομένους, ἔρημος ἁγία προσηγόρευτο. Κάδης γὰρ ἑρμηνεύεται ἡ ἁγία. Αὕτη ἡ φωνὴ καταρτίζει καὶ ἐλά-φους, τὰς ἁγίας ψυχὰς, τὰς τὰ ὑψηλὰ ζητούσας, τὰς τῶν ὄφεων δαπανητικὰς, τὰς ἐπὶ τῶν ὑψηλῶν ὀρέων τὴν διατριβὴν ποιουμένας. Αὗται δ' ἂν εἶεν ψυχαὶ μεγαλοφυεῖς, ἐπὶ τὰ ὑψηλὰ τῆς κατ' οὐρανὸν πολιτείας ἐκ τῶν ταπεινῶν ἀνατρέχουσαι, κοῦφαι καὶ διηρμέναι· πόλεμον ἔχουσαι πρὸς τὰς ἀντικειμένας δυνάμεις, ὡς πρὸς τοὺς ὄφεις αἱ ἔλαφοι. Ἀλλὰ Καὶ ἀποκαλύπτει δρυμοὺς, ἵνα οἱ ὄφεις φανεροὶ γένωνται, οἱ ὑπὸ τοῦ συσκιασμοῦ τῶν δρυμῶν καλυπτόμενοι, πρὸς τὸ ἀπονώτερον αὐτοὺς ὑπὸ τῶν ἐλάφων καταναλίσκεσθαι. Τάχα οὖν ὁ ἐλέγχων τὰς ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ κακίας, ἀποκαλύπτει δρυμούς· τουτέστιν, εἰς ἐμφανὲς ἄγει τὰς ἐμφωλευούσας τῇ ὑλικῇ φύσει ἁμαρτίας, ὄφεις λεγομένας διὰ τὸ ποικίλον τῆς ἡδονῆς. Ἀποκαλύψει δὲ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ, ὅτε ἀποκαλύψει τὰ κρυπτὰ τοῦ σκότους, καὶ τὰς βουλὰς τῶν καρδιῶν αὐτῶν. Τάχα δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰωάννης, φωνὴ ὢν τοῦ Κυρίου, ἐν αἰνίγματι τῷ Ἰσραὴλ διελέγετο, ὅτι Ἤδη ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται. Πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν, ἐκκόπτεται, καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται. Ἀπεκάλυπτε τοὺς δρυμοὺς, τουτέστι τῶν καρπῶν τὸ ἄχρηστον ἐφανέρου· ἄκαρπος γὰρ ὕλη ὁ δρυμός. Οὗ τὸ βλαβερὸν ἐπιδεικνύων αὐτοῖς, εἰς τὴν ἐπιβάλλουσαν καρπογονίαν προσεκαλεῖτο, λέγων· Ποιήσατε τοὺς καρποὺς ἀξίους τῆς μετανοίας. Ἐξ ὧν πάντων ἕν ἐστιν ἀποτέλεσμα, τὸ οἰκοδομηθῆναι τὸν ναὸν Κυρίου, ἔνθα πᾶς ὁ γενόμενος δύναται ἀληθῶς ἐνεγκεῖν τῷ Κυρίῳ δόξαν. Ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ Κύριος τὸν κατακλυσμὸν κατοικιεῖ. Διὰ γὰρ τοῦ βαπτίσματος ἡ εἰς τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἡγιασμένων τοῦ Κυρίου κατοίκησις. Τὴν οὖν ἀπολουομένην τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ψυχὴν, ταύτην κατοικεῖ ὁ Θεός. Διὰ τοῦτο λέγεται τὸν κατακλυσμὸν κατοικεῖν. Ὅτι γὰρ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ βαπτίσματος ἄφεσιν κα-τακλυσμὸν προσηγόρευσε, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ τριακοστοῦ πρώτου ψαλμοῦ μεμαθήκαμεν, ἐν τῷ εἰπεῖν· Πλὴν ἐν κατακλυσμῷ ὑδάτων πολλῶν πρὸς αὐτὸν οὐκ ἐγγιοῦσιν. Αἱ γὰρ ἁμαρτίαι τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν, ἐν τῇ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος ἀπολυτρώσει, ὡς προσεγγίζειν οὐκέτι συγχωρηθήσονται. Καὶ καθιεῖται Κύριος βασιλεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Ἐπὶ πᾶσι τούτοις ὑπάρξει ἡμῖν γνωρίσαι τὴν ἐπὶ πάντων ἀρχὴν τοῦ Δεσπότου, τοῦ διδόντος ἰσχὺν τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα νικήσαντες τὸν πονηρὸν, τὴν εὐλογίαν χωρήσωμεν τὴν διδομένην ὑπὸ Κυρίου ἐν εἰρήνῃ τοῖς ἀξίοις αὐτοῦ· ὅτι αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The voice exposes hidden sins and the Lord dwells through baptism
orientation: Basil continues his interpretation of Psalm 28, explaining how the voice of the Lord—John the Baptist—shakes the desert, reveals hidden sins, and how the Lord dwells in purified souls through baptism.
pass_a_gloss: That flame, therefore, he was cutting through by bringing the fearful things before the eyes of the people. And the Lord will shake the desert of Kadesh. For John was baptizing in the desert. That desert, therefore, he shook by the arrival of the peoples from everywhere; which desert, because those coming repented, was called holy desert. For Kadesh is interpreted as the holy one. This voice also perfects deer, the holy souls, the ones seeking the high things, the ones destructive of serpents, the ones making their dwelling on the high mountains. These would be great-souled souls, running up to the high things of the heavenly citizenship from the lowly things, light and lifted up; having war against the opposing powers, as deer have against serpents. But also he reveals forests, so that the serpents may become visible, the ones hidden by the shade of the forests, for the purpose of their being consumed by the deer with less labor. Perhaps, therefore, the one who refutes the evils in secret reveals forests; that is, he brings into the open the sins lurking in the material nature, called serpents because of the varied character of pleasure. And he will reveal in the day, when he will reveal the hidden things of darkness and the counsels of their hearts. Perhaps also John, being the voice of the Lord, spoke to Israel in a riddle, that Already the axe lies at the root of the trees. Every tree, therefore, not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire. He was revealing the forests, that is, he was making manifest the uselessness of the fruits; for the forest is fruitless wood. Showing to them its harmfulness, he was summoning them to the fruit-bearing that was incumbent upon them, saying: Produce fruits worthy of repentance. From all these things there is one result, that the temple of the Lord be built, where everyone who enters can truly bring glory to the Lord. But also the Lord will inhabit the flood. For through baptism is the dwelling of the Lord in the souls of the sanctified. The soul, therefore, that washes away sin, this soul God inhabits. For this reason it is said that he inhabits the flood. For that he called the forgiveness from baptism a flood, we have learned also from the thirty-first psalm, in the saying: Surely in a flood of many waters they will not draw near to him. For the sins of sinners, in the redemption through baptism, will no longer be permitted to draw near. And the Lord will sit as king forever. Upon all these things it will be ours to know the rule over all things of the Master, who gives strength to his people, so that having conquered the evil one, we may receive the blessing given by the Lord in peace to those worthy of him; because to him be the glory unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: The comparative of ἄπονος means 'with less toil' or 'more effortlessly'; 'more easily' loses the labor/effort nuance.

choices.english: Surely in a flood of many waters
choices.why: Πλήν here introduces a strong affirmation or contrast, not a restriction; 'Surely' or 'Indeed' captures the sense that in the flood sins will not approach.
The verb means to complete, equip, or make fit; 'perfects' conveys the sense of bringing the holy souls to completion.
The verb means to lie hidden in a den or lair; 'lurking in' captures the hidden, den-like quality of sins in material nature.
The verb κατοικίζω means to settle or cause to dwell; 'will inhabit' preserves the active dwelling of the Lord in souls.
The verb χωρέω here means to make room for or receive; 'may receive' captures the sense of being granted the blessing.

pass_b_english: So he was cutting through that flame by bringing the terrible things before the people's eyes. “The Lord will shake the desert of Kadesh” (Psalm 28:8 LXX). For John was baptizing in the desert. He shook that desert by the arrival of peoples from every direction, which, because those who came repented, was called holy desert. For Kadesh means “holy.” This voice also perfects the deer—the holy souls who seek the heights, who destroy serpents, who make their dwelling on the high mountains. These would be great-souled souls, running up from lowly things to the heights of the heavenly way of life, light and lifted up, waging war against the opposing powers just as deer wage war against serpents. But it also reveals forests, so that the serpents hidden by the shade of the forests become visible, and the deer can consume them with less labor. Perhaps, then, the one who exposes the evils done in secret reveals forests—that is, he brings into the open the sins lurking in material nature, which are called serpents because of the many-colored character of pleasure. And he will reveal them in the day when he will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and the purposes of their hearts. Perhaps John too, being the voice of the Lord, spoke to Israel in a riddle: “Already the axe is laid at the root of the trees. Every tree therefore that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire” (Luke 3:9). He was revealing the forests—that is, he was exposing the uselessness of fruits, for a forest is fruitless timber. By showing them its harmful character, he was summoning them to the fruit-bearing that was required of them, saying, “Bear fruits worthy of repentance” (Matthew 3:8). From all these things there is one result: the building of the temple of the Lord, where everyone who is constituted there can truly bring glory to the Lord. But also, “the Lord will inhabit the flood.” For through baptism the Lord comes to dwell in the souls of his sanctified ones. God inhabits the soul that is being washed clean of sin. For this reason it is said that he inhabits the flood. That Scripture calls the forgiveness that comes from baptism a flood we have also learned from the thirty-first psalm, where it says, “Surely in a flood of many waters they will not draw near to him” (Psalm 31:6 LXX). For the sins of sinners, in the redemption that comes through baptism, will no longer be permitted to approach him. “And the Lord will sit as king forever” (Psalm 28:10 LXX). After all these things, it remains for us to acknowledge the rule of the Master over all things, who gives strength to his people, so that having conquered the evil one, we may receive the blessing given by the Lord in peace to those who are worthy of him. For to him be glory forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: He shook that desert by the arrival of peoples from every direction, and because those who came repented, the desert was called holy.
problems.source_quote: Τὴν ἔρημον οὖν ἐκείνην συνέσεισε τῇ ἐπιδημίᾳ τῶν πανταχόθεν λαῶν· ἥτις, διὰ τὸ μετανοεῖν τοὺς ἐρχομένους, ἔρημος ἁγία προσηγόρευτο.
problems.why: Agency and syntax wrong: John shook the desert by the peoples' arrival; the relative clause 'which, because those coming repented, was called holy desert' refers to the desert, not a separate 'and' clause.
problems.fix: He shook that desert by the sojourn of peoples from every direction, which, because those who came repented, was called holy desert.

problems.quote: So he was cutting through that flame by bringing the people face to face with what they feared.
problems.source_quote: Ἐκείνην οὖν τὴν φλόγα διέκοπτε τῷ ὑπ' ὄψιν ἄγειν τὰ φοβερὰ τῷ λαῷ.
problems.why: Subject is wrong: source says 'he was cutting through that flame by bringing the terrible things before the people's eyes'—referring to Moses showing the calf-ground-to-powder to Israel, not 'bringing people face to face with what they feared.'
problems.fix: So he was cutting through that flame by bringing the terrible things before the people's eyes.
problems.ruling: τῷ λαῷ is dative of reference; τὰ φοβερὰ are the fearful things shown to the people, not people shown what they feared.

problems.quote: where everyone who enters can truly give glory to the Lord
problems.source_quote: ἔνθα πᾶς ὁ γενόμενος δύναται ἀληθῶς ἐνεγκεῖν τῷ Κυρίῳ δόξαν
problems.why: 'Enters' is wrong: ὁ γενόμενος means 'everyone who becomes/comes to be' (in the temple, i.e., is formed as a Christian), not 'enters.'
problems.fix: where everyone who is formed can truly bring glory to the Lord
problems.ruling: ὁ γενόμενος means 'who comes to be/becomes,' not 'enters'; mistranslates the verb's core meaning.

problems.quote: God inhabits the soul that washes away its sin.
problems.source_quote: Τὴν οὖν ἀπολουομένην τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ψυχὴν, ταύτην κατοικεῖ ὁ Θεός
problems.why: Middle voice misread: ἀπολουομένην is passive 'being washed clean of sin,' not active 'washes away its sin.' The soul is washed, not doing the washing.
problems.fix: God inhabits the soul that is being washed clean of sin.
problems.ruling: ἀπολουομένην is passive 'being washed' of sin, not active 'washes away its sin'; voice and agency reversed.

edits.new: So he was cutting through that flame by bringing the terrible things before the people's eyes.

edits.old: He shook that desert by the arrival of peoples from every direction, and because those who came repented, the desert was called holy.
edits.new: He shook that desert by the arrival of peoples from every direction, which, because those who came repented, was called holy desert.

edits.new: where everyone who is formed can truly bring glory to the Lord

edits.old: God inhabits the soul that washes away its sin.

fixed: Corrected subject and object: source says he brought the fearful things before the people's eyes, not the people face to face with what they feared.
Corrected syntax: the relative clause refers to the desert, not a separate clause; restored 'holy desert' as the predicate.
Corrected ὁ γενόμενος to 'is formed' rather than 'enters'; also adjusted 'give' to 'bring' to match ἐνεγκεῖν.
Corrected middle/passive voice: the soul is being washed clean, not washing itself.

problems.why: τὸ ἄχρηστον means 'the uselessness' but 'their fruits' is wrong: τῶν καρπῶν is genitive, but the sense is 'the uselessness of fruits' in general or 'that fruits are useless', not specifically 'their fruits'.
ὁ γενόμενος means 'everyone who comes to be' or 'everyone who becomes' (a Christian, purified, etc.), not 'formed' as in shaped/created.
problems.fix: everyone who comes to be there
problems.ruling: γενόμενος means 'who comes to be/becomes', not 'formed'; mistranslates, misleading reader.

edits.new: everyone who comes to be there

fixed: τῶν καρπῶν τὸ ἄχρηστον: the genitive is general, not possessive 'their'; changed to 'the uselessness of fruits'.
πᾶς ὁ γενόμενος: means 'everyone who comes to be', not 'formed'; changed to 'everyone who comes to be there'.

problems.quote: where everyone who comes to be there can truly bring glory to the Lord
problems.source_quote: ἔνθα πᾶς ὁ γενόμενος δύναται ἀληθῶς ἐνεγκεῖν τῷ Κυρίῳ δόξαν
problems.why: ὁ γενόμενος means 'everyone who comes to be [in it]', i.e., who is made/constituted there (in the temple), not 'comes to be there' as in arrives. It suggests spiritual formation/constitution in the temple.
problems.fix: where everyone who is constituted there can truly bring glory to the Lord

problems.source_quote: Ἤδη ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται. Πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλόν, ἐκκόπτεται, καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
problems.why: Basil attributes this to John the Baptist as 'voice of the Lord' speaking in riddles; but the citation format '(Matthew 3:10)' is added by translator. The Greek quotes match Luke 3:9, not Matthew 3:10 (Matthew has 'ἤδη γὰρ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται' with γάρ; Luke 3:9 matches exactly).
problems.ruling: Greek text omits γάρ matching Luke 3:9 exactly, not Matthew 3:10 which has γάρ. Wrong reference.

problems.source_quote: ἡ εἰς τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἡγιασμένων τοῦ Κυρίου κατοίκησις
problems.why: τοῦ Κυρίου is genitive with ἡγιασμένων: 'the sanctified of the Lord' or 'the Lord's sanctified ones', not 'the Lord comes to dwell'. The dwelling is in the souls of the Lord's sanctified ones.
problems.fix: through baptism the dwelling of the Lord comes to be in the souls of his sanctified ones
problems.ruling: τοῦ Κυρίου is objective genitive with κατοίκησις: 'the Lord's dwelling' in souls, not 'Lord comes to dwell.'

Adjusted 'the sanctified' to 'his sanctified ones' to reflect the genitive τοῦ Κυρίου modifying ἡγιασμένων.
